::::{#exm-smoothing-spline-large-penalty}

#### A heavily penalized smoothing spline matches the least-squares line

In the built-in `cars` data,
the code below fits a smoothing spline of stopping distance on speed with a very large penalty,
and compares its fitted values with those of the least-squares line:

```{r}
#| label: exm-ss-large-penalty
cars_lm <- lm(dist ~ speed, data = cars)
cars_big_lambda <- smooth.spline(cars$speed, cars$dist, lambda = 1e6)
max_gap <- max(abs(predict(cars_big_lambda, cars$speed)$y - fitted(cars_lm)))
```

The largest gap between the two sets of fitted values is `r format(max_gap, digits = 2)`,
which is negligible next to stopping distances measured in feet,
as @thm-smoothing-spline-large-penalty says.
